upstream: hexstrike-ai (0x4m4), pinned d689933 — vendored NON-runnable; 79 distinct external tools
note: fact_capable is set ONLY when a runner-owned oracle re-drive exists AND the ToolSpec passes the conformance battery (live.conformance). Everything else is LEAD-only or excluded. The count that matters is fact_capable, not the upstream tool count. Two FACT families are VIGIL-DIRECT (no tool is the authority): VERSION_RANGE via live.sbom (SBOM/dependency-CVE) and ACHIEVED_STATE via live.web_redrive — both HEADER-DERIVED (3xx Location, CORS headers, OIDC via Location) and BODY-DERIVED evidence. Body-derived branches are FACT-capable: the capture reverses Content-Encoding and determines the charset the way a browser does (integration/vigil_integration/live/body_decode.py — complete single-member gzip/deflate + the WHATWG encoding map), and the JS-redirect branch mints only from executable code, decided by a real tokenizer (engine/crucible/framework/v2/scanner/js_lex.py:sink_is_executable), not a regex. They remain NOT CLEAN-capable, for a different reason than the decode: a non-firing cannot distinguish 'the document declares no redirect' from 'we could not read the document', and lexing cannot prove a runtime-assembled sink absent. An undeclared charset, brotli/zstd, concatenated members and truncated reads are INCONCLUSIVE, and no-channel is INCONCLUSIVE not CLEAN. Their proposer tools (trivy/grype, httpx) keep fact_capable=false by design.

tools.name: nmap
tools.notes: runner re-drives its own gated TCP handshake; service_reachable FACT. NPSL restricts commercial redistribution.

tools.name: masscan
tools.notes: H5 SERVICE_REACHABILITY reuse: runner re-drives its OWN gated TCP handshake per proposed port (the SAME service_reachability.tcp_handshake branch as nmap); the scanner is only a port PROPOSER and its output is never the FACT authority. Flags are built server-side from a strict ports schema. masscan sends raw SYN packets and normally needs root (privileges=sometimes).

Flags are built server-side from a strict ports schema. Run with -silent and -host so only results print and the target is a flag value, not a positional that could be read as a flag.

tools.name: zmap
tools.notes: H5 batch 2 SERVICE_REACHABILITY reuse (W1 promotion): runner re-drives its OWN gated TCP handshake per proposed port (the SAME service_reachability.tcp_handshake branch as nmap/masscan); the scanner is only a single-port PROPOSER and its output is never the FACT authority. build_argv is server-side (zmap -p <one port> -q -o - <target>; the port is a strict single-value schema, never model-supplied) and the parser pins the host to the scope-authorised target. Wired FACT-capable via the R4 runner (brains.hexstrike_body._spec_for_kind builds zmap_service_scan(fact_capable=True), so the empty-redrive spec routes to the FACT-capable twin) and passes live.conformance.run_toolspec_conformance; no new oracle, no new FACT branch. The default-mode (fact_capable=False) spec still admits to the LEAD-only hexstrike.service_reachability branch. HONESTY: zmap needs raw-socket root, so the presence probe reports it fact-capable-but-proposer-UNAVAILABLE in a sandbox without CAP_NET_RAW (never a false EXECUTABLE); the connect()-based FACT re-drive needs no raw socket and is unaffected.

tools.name: unicornscan
tools.notes: H5 batch 2 SERVICE_REACHABILITY reuse (W1 promotion): runner re-drives its OWN gated TCP handshake per proposed port (the SAME service_reachability.tcp_handshake branch as nmap/masscan); the scanner is only a port PROPOSER and its output is never the FACT authority. build_argv is server-side (unicornscan -mT <target>:<ports>; ports are a strict validated schema, never model-supplied) and the parser takes only the bracketed open port, pinning the host to the scope-authorised target. Wired FACT-capable via the R4 runner (brains.hexstrike_body._spec_for_kind builds unicornscan_service_scan(fact_capable=True), so the empty-redrive spec routes to the FACT-capable twin) and passes live.conformance.run_toolspec_conformance; no new oracle, no new FACT branch. The default-mode (fact_capable=False) spec still admits to the LEAD-only hexstrike.service_reachability branch. HONESTY: unicornscan sends raw packets and needs root, so the presence probe reports it fact-capable-but-proposer-UNAVAILABLE in a sandbox without CAP_NET_RAW (never a false EXECUTABLE); the connect()-based FACT re-drive needs no raw socket and is unaffected.

tools.name: sslscan

tools.name: httpx
tools.notes: HexStrike W2 endpoint-LIVENESS FACT (the L7 analogue of SERVICE_REACHABILITY): httpx PROPOSES a URL and VIGIL re-drives it with its OWN plain gated GET plus TWO SAME-SHAPE not-found CONTROLS (same character class / length / extension as the target's last path segment, randomized); the predicate_oracle mints a signed achieved_state.endpoint_liveness FACT only when the target is 2xx/3xx and is distinguishable from a stable same-shape not-found baseline (different status, or same status with a stable control body the target differs from), so a soft-404 / numeric-route / shape-signature / path-echo server mints NO fact (a LEAD), and a root/directory URL with no mirrorable segment fails closed to a LEAD. The tool's URL row is only a proposer; VIGIL's own gated GET is the fact authority. HTTP exposure is re-derived by VIGIL's live.web_redrive ACHIEVED_STATE path (no install): VIGIL issues its OWN gated, no-redirect capture and the deterministic predicate_oracle adjudicates — the tool is only a URL proposer, never the fact authority for the exposure classes. CAPABILITY BOUNDARY (honest, narrower than the family name): HEADER-DERIVED evidence — a 3xx Location host, CORS reflected-origin-with-credentials, an OIDC redirect proven through Location — is both FACT- and CLEAN-capable. BODY-DERIVED branches (meta-refresh / body redirect, host-header reflected into HTML, the JS redirect sink) are FACT-capable but NOT CLEAN-capable. The decode gap that once made them unsound is CLOSED: integration/vigil_integration/live/body_decode.py reverses Content-Encoding (a complete, single-member, bounded gzip/deflate stream) and determines the charset the way a browser does (BOM, then the transport Content-Type label resolved through the WHATWG encoding map, strict decode), and body_semantically_available gates every body-dependent predicate — so an undeclared charset, a brotli/zstd body, concatenated members or a truncated read yield INCONCLUSIVE instead of a CLEAN over a document VIGIL never read. The JS-redirect branch mints only from EXECUTABLE code, decided by a real tokenizer (engine/crucible/framework/v2/scanner/js_lex.py:sink_is_executable — comments, string/template literals and ambiguous /-spans are excluded structurally), so it is FACT-capable rather than LEAD-only. What keeps the body branches from CLEAN is no longer decoding but ABSENCE: a non-firing cannot distinguish 'the document declares no redirect' from 'we could not read this document', and lexing cannot prove a runtime-assembled sink absent (that needs DOM rendering, which is not wired). Per-branch limitations and blocking_work are in docs/capability-matrix/evidence-branches.json, which governs admission.
